bull_case: AI accelerators, custom silicon, smartphones and advanced packaging all expand the value captured by leading-edge foundry capacity.
bear_case: Foundry rivals, customer insourcing, export controls or a slower AI capex cycle can reduce the duration of excess demand.
thesis: TSMC is not a disruptive entrant, but it is a foundational enabler of the AI compute transition. N2/A16, CoWoS/3DFabric and leading-edge yield/capacity economics shape the performance frontier for many semiconductor customers.

evidence.claim: 2025 advanced technologies were 74% of wafer revenue.
2Q26 advanced nodes were 77% of wafer revenue, including 2nm at 3%.

counterevidence: Overseas fabs carry structurally higher costs; customer concentration and Taiwan/export-control tail risks remain material.
unknowns: AI/HPC demand duration beyond the current capacity-constrained cycle
falsifiers: A sustained loss of leading-edge share, repeated yield delays, or owner FCF/share stagnation despite rising capex would weaken the thesis.

key_kpis.name: owner FCF/share
key_kpis.threshold: sustained growth through the capex cycle

next_checks: 3Q26 results, N2 ramp, CoWoS/advanced packaging capacity, overseas-fab margin, top-customer concentration

subscores.rationale: TSMC's leading-edge scaling and advanced packaging enable step-function compute density and energy efficiency.
2Q26 advanced nodes were 77% of wafer revenue and 2nm already contributed 3% during initial ramp.
Logic scaling, advanced packaging, specialty nodes and global manufacturing create multiple adjacent value pools and industry standards.

uncertainties.rationale: AI-cycle duration, overseas economics and geopolitical/customer concentration remain material uncertainties.
